Datamimic Review: Stop Coding Agents from Inventing Test Fixtures
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title frontloads the product (DATAMIMIC) and names the reader problem in plain words: test data a coding agent should not invent itself. 'Validate' is the mechanism the article actually documents - a declarative model run through datamimic scaffold until it returns verified=true - so the promise matches the tested path instead of the retired, absolute 'Invent Its Own Test World' framing. At 56 characters it survives search and social truncation, and it drops the year label that added no information.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover is a title card, not a data plot: it restates the reviewed headline ('Datamimic Review' with the subtitle 'Validate Your Coding Agent's Test Data') on the site's existing dark grid template. It carries no numbers, no benchmark bars and no vendor claims, so nothing in it can be mistaken for measured evidence; its only job is to keep the visible article title consistent with the frontmatter and schema headline.
